newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: FORECAST - Half yr profit slump seen for Air NZ.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Half yr profit slump seen for Air NZ.

text.p: Strength in the New Zealand dollar, particularly against the yen, and high jet fuel prices are expected to slash Air New Zealand's first half earnings when it reports on Wednesday.
Analysts expect a net profit of around NZ$75 million for the six months to December, down from NZ$135.1 million a year ago.

"It's basically going to be a terrible interim because of all the things the market knows about -- the slow growth out of Asia, fuel prices, and the currency has really moved strongly against them," said one analyst, who declined to be named.

But analysts said there were signs that Air NZ had gone through the worst, with fuel prices easing, less competitive pressure on trans-Tasman routes and its recent 3.0 percent fare increase, although the latter would take time to flow through.
Anecdotal evidence suggested January was very strong plus the demise of cut price rival Kiwi International may also have an impact.

Looking ahead, analysts said the alliance with UAL's United Airlines should start to bear fruit now that air travel in the U.S. has ceased to be dominated by domestic business stirred up by the Atlanta Olympics.
Analysts also expect a progress report on "project save" - the campaign to shave NZ$100 million off costs, plus plans for any future possible alliances.

Yasmin Allen ANZ Securities in Sydney expects NZ75.6 million net profit. Ansett Airlines, which made an operating loss before tax of A$18.6 million in the year to June, was expected to make a small contribution since Air NZ's purchase of a half share became effective on October 1.
Allen estimated the impact of the strong currency affected pre-tax profits by 48 percent, but agreed Air New Zealand appeared to be at a turning point.
She expected currency-related benefits to kick in over 1998 and 1999 and that Air NZ would benefit from an expected turnaround in Ansett over those same years.
ANZ Securities rates Air NZ as a long term buy, short term hold. The brokerage may look to upgrade Air NZ to a short term buy, depending on the strength of the result, she said.
Allen said she would be looking for evidence of synergies between Air NZ and Ansett and how much Air NZ had offset costs.
"If they've getting cost savings through, then that will have leverage out to 1998, obviously if the currency does turn around," she said. "But I think Ansett is the key going forward," Allen said.
